title: Proteomic profiling of obesity-associated metabolic and immune changes in Göttingen minipigs
projectDescription: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for increased severity following influenza A virus (IAV) infection, likely through meta-inflammation and immune dysregulation. The mechanisms by which obesity alters antiviral and inflammatory responses remain poorly understood. Using a diet-induced obesity model in Göttingen minipigs, we compared immune and inflammatory responses between obese and lean animals before and after IAV infection. While uninfected pigs showed no clear obesity-associated immune or histological changes in the respiratory tract, obese pigs exhibited reduced viral clearance, altered antiviral gene expression, and increased cellular infiltration post-infection, alongside elevated C-reactive protein levels. This indicates that innate antiviral immunity is affected post-infection in obese animals, potentially contributing to more severe influenza outcomes. The proteomics dataset included here, however, reflects only the obese versus lean state prior to infection, providing insights into baseline metabolic and inflammatory differences. This model demonstrates high translational value for studying obesity-associated immune modulation.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Tissue samples were homogenized in lysis buffer (6 M GuHCl, 10 mM TCEP, 40 mM CAA, 50 mM HEPES pH 8.5, protease inhibitors) using a TissueLyser II. Lysates were heated at 95°C, precipitated in acetone overnight at -20°C, centrifuged, and resuspended. Protein concentration was determined by BCA assay. Proteins (20 µg) were digested sequentially with LysC (1:50, 4 h) and trypsin (1:100, overnight) at 37°C, acidified with 2% TFA, and peptides cleaned using EvoSep stage tips.  Peptides were separated on EvoSep One over a 58-min gradient (“20 samples per day” method) with no further enrichment. MS analysis was performed on an Orbitrap Exploris in DIA mode with FAIMS (CV -45 V). Full MS spectra were acquired at 120,000 resolution (400–1350 m/z) and MS2 at 15,000 resolution (HCD 33, 20 m/z window with 1 m/z overlap, 3 s cycle). Performance was monitored with QC standards and chromatography reproducibility.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw DIA files were analyzed using Spectronaut™ v18.6 (Biognosys) against the Sus scrofa UniProt database (UP000008227). Dynamic modifications included Oxidation (M) and N-terminal acetylation, with Carbamidomethylation (C) set as static. Identifications were filtered at 1% FDR, and only proteotypic peptides were used for protein quantification at the M21 level. Protein groups were inferred using IDPicker, and default DIA parameters were applied (20 m/z isolation windows with 1 m/z overlap, normalized HCD collision energy 33, FAIMS CV -45 V).  Quantitative and statistical analysis was performed in RStudio v4.4.1. Protein intensities were log2-transformed and checked for normality. Differential abundance between groups was assessed using t-tests, with p-values corrected for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Data quality and reproducibility were verified using principal component analysis and inspection of peptide intensity distributions.
